fields.Core Themes JSON: [{"title": "The Final Experiment Under the Microscope", "body": "Chance Garton opens with the wave of headlines announcing that flat-earthers had reverted to the globe, and Steve Falconer argues the Antarctic trip was never an experiment at all: no control, no certainty about where the group actually stood, and no proof the light they filmed was the sun. He notes that Austin, the other flat-earth traveler, did not change his position and is almost never mentioned in the coverage. Falconer says he has since read Antarctic expedition journals from the late 1500s to the mid 1900s and found no mention of a 24-hour sun, only night, dusk and next morning."}, {"title": "One Fact Cannot Cancel Another", "body": "Chance reads a passage from the old Zetetic Astronomy book that Falconer had used in his first film, arguing that one fact can never contradict another and that both must be true. Falconer builds his answer around it, contending that a light in the sky over Antarctica cannot erase the lock and canal engineering he cites through New York State, Rochester and the Suez Canal, where he argues a roughly 630 foot cascade of curvature would be required and is absent. He also points to English law books that he says instruct engineers to assume a flat datum line and a plumb line."}, {"title": "Why Falconer Thinks the Model Is Guarded", "body": "Asked whether Antarctica functions as an inverted tower of Babel, with nations gathering at the periphery to obscure rather than seek the truth, Falconer contends the stakes are physics, religion and money at once. He argues everything is a toroidal field and that light is a perturbation in the ether, so a sealed perimeter would take Newtonian particle physics down with it. He contends that the Vatican's Unam Sanctam bull and the Gregorian calendar underwrite a copyright over name, date and place, comparing the all caps straw man to performing as Harry Potter and owing the author. He points listeners to Stephen Young's Fool's Wisdom."}, {"title": "Day Lengths, Latitude Rings and Sun Trackers", "body": "In the middle stretch Falconer describes auditing sunrise, sunset and day length figures for Antarctic stations across Wikipedia, Google Earth, Stellarium and time and date sites. He says three or four sources can disagree about the very same base, differing on when its 24-hour sun begins by anywhere from two days to about twenty-five, with one outlier he threw out after tracing it to two stations with similar names. He argues that matching latitudes north and south should share day lengths and do not. Chance adds that clock time and time zones impose uniformity while dividing people from one another."}, {"title": "Mapping the Bases and the Old Expeditions", "body": "For the final stretch Falconer previews part three of Scamtarctica, made with a mapmaker named Rob and his returning Spacebusters partner Ross, plotting stations and expedition tracks onto Alex Gleason's flat map. He raises the SANAE IV knife story, where a crew was reported stranded for 190 days although Troll Station and other bases sit within a couple hundred miles on the globe, and argues those gaps widen along an ice wall perimeter. He questions the South Pole base location against Scott's journal coordinates, notes that the round-Antarctica yacht race stops at Cape Town, India and Australia, and blames phone magnets for the trip's compass trouble."}]
fields.Intro Paragraph 1: In this reality-rattling episode, Steve Falconer of Spacebusters joins InnerVerse to challenge the official story of Antarctica, and with it, the entire cosmological structure we've been taught to trust.
fields.Intro Paragraph 2: We break down the "Final Experiment" video and its deception, why sun observations at Antarctic bases don't match any globe model, zetetic science versus Newtonian illusion, the mystery of maps, magnetic anomalies and missing circumnavigations, and how spiritual sovereignty connects to cosmic awareness. Steve peels back layers of illusion, geographic, scientific and metaphysical, to reveal a world far stranger and more sacred than we've been led to believe. Whether you're globe-weary or just hungry for deeper knowing, this episode is a metaphysical expedition you won't forget.

fields.Plus Core Themes JSON: [{"title": "The Sun as a Traveling Wave, Not a Fireball", "body": "Steve lays out a wave based model where the sun is not a burning ball hanging in a void but the visible tail end of a much faster vibration traveling through a toroidal field. He compares it to a bullwhip crack, where the motion at the tip is slow compared to the source, and to a guitar amp heard at different distances inside a stadium. Standing on a lakeshore at sunset, every viewer sees the light trail reach only their own feet, which he offers as proof that each person intersects the same traveling wave from a different angle rather than watching one distant burning object."}, {"title": "Dielectric Centers, Magnetism, and the Shape of Reality", "body": "Steve describes a toroidal field model in which a dielectric center perpetually spits magnetism out and sucks it back in, with the slowest moving plane of inertia sitting at the middle, the flat earth, sandwiched between two mirrored funnels. The sun and moon are framed as magnets whose interplay produces eclipses and phases, and the ice wall sits at the outer edge where nature thins out, since neither the exact center nor the extreme edge of a magnetic field supports life. He also offers his own unproven theory that compasses grow erratic near the ice wall because travelers sit too far from the northern dielectric to be pulled reliably."}, {"title": "Tesla, Walter Russell, and Sound as the Root of Light", "body": "Drawing on Tesla's line that the secrets of the universe are found in energy, frequency and vibration, Steve argues that sound collapsing in the ether becomes visible light, with color and form simply different frequencies of the same vibration, like a dog whistle pitched beyond human hearing. He layers in Walter Russell's idea of a still white magnetic light as the body of a thinking, intelligent mind he calls God, and rereads Genesis through that lens, arguing the formless void and the word spoken over the waters describe sound collapsing into form rather than a literal story about water and darkness."}, {"title": "Mirror Worlds and the Limits of Certainty", "body": "Prompted by a question about what lies on the far side of the flat disc, Steve speculates about an inverted, mirrored earth with its own sun and moon, tying it to myths of an underworld, the show Stranger Things and the fact that the eye's own image arrives flipped in the brain. He frames this as personal theory rather than settled fact, insisting nobody truly knows how the realm works, and he later extends the same humility to his idea about compasses malfunctioning near the ice wall, offering it only as a hunch drawn from his toroidal field model rather than a proven mechanism."}, {"title": "Releasing the Need to Win the Argument", "body": "Both voices describe moving past the exhausting work of trying to convert skeptics, choosing instead to speak plainly with the curious and think deeply with the wise, and to let the world be deceived if it insists on it. Chance reframes this as a centric cosmology that puts faith in one's own relationship to source light rather than in winning debates, arguing that a mind held in coherence quietly entrains the disorder around it the way scattered metronomes fall into rhythm. Steve closes by tying identity to history, insisting that not knowing where you live or where you came from leaves you unable to know where you are going."}]

Nobody has ever mentioned a 24-hour sun.", "author": "Steve Falconer", "portrait": "https://images.squarespace-cdn.com/content/5987d897cf81e0278ec5322e/f8e002bb-ad0c-479e-8907-31541f55ff2d/STEVE-FALCONER.jpg?content-type=image%2Fjpeg"}, {"text": "The nations are uniting, but not to find enlightenment and raise up to the center to seek God and truth, but they're actually at the periphery to obscure the truth.", "author": "Chance Garton", "portrait": "https://images.squarespace-cdn.com/content/5987d897cf81e0278ec5322e/a784fd99-3e6f-436c-a8f3-c4f913b855ed/profile-pic.jpg?content-type=image%2Fjpeg"}, {"text": "That's what we're doing, we're going out pretending to be our all caps name on a fake spinning ball in a fake universe that doesn't exist on a fake calendar that doesn't exist.", "author": "Steve Falconer", "portrait": "https://images.squarespace-cdn.com/content/5987d897cf81e0278ec5322e/f8e002bb-ad0c-479e-8907-31541f55ff2d/STEVE-FALCONER.jpg?content-type=image%2Fjpeg"}, {"text": "It's wild how much of the modern world's construction creates uniformity, as in forces everybody to do the same thing, but yet divides everybody from each other.", "author": "Chance Garton", "portrait": "https://images.squarespace-cdn.com/content/5987d897cf81e0278ec5322e/a784fd99-3e6f-436c-a8f3-c4f913b855ed/profile-pic.jpg?content-type=image%2Fjpeg"}, {"text": "I found no, not a one, not even on the same base.
